source.title: Insights on representational similarity in neural networks with canonical correlation
source.authors: Ari S. Morcos; M. Raghu; Samy Bengio

record.tranche_reason: The study trains CIFAR-10 networks on fixed random labels and reports near-zero training loss, directly applying the random-label training intervention relevant to V1.
record.gate_note: The paper reports near-zero training loss for networks trained on true or random labels. Its CCA distances compare representations and do not measure the claim versions directly; figure-only CCA values are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study itself trains five CIFAR-10 CNNs on a fixed random labeling and reports near-zero training loss, directly testing V1's fitting result. Section 3.1 specifies identical topology; Appendix A.4 gives a common Adam training procedure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for Section 3.1: random-label networks achieve near-zero training loss, and their later hidden-layer representations are less similar across runs than those of true-label networks. Both groups have highly similar softmax representations on training data; only true-label networks have similar softmax representations on test data.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CIFAR-10 networks and fixed randomized labels, with training details referring to an earlier setup; the paper measures representational similarity rather than focusing on fitting performance.
record.method_sensitivity: The representational similarity result varies by layer; at the softmax, the groups are highly similar when measured on training data, while only true-label networks converge to similar outputs on test data.

fits_no_version.finding: True-label networks have more similar later-layer representations across initializations than random-label networks; early-layer similarities are comparable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-label memorization produces more diverse converged later-layer representations than true-label learning. This does not establish V6's temporal ordering.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-related representation components stabilize before components described as representational noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Useful representations stabilize before other representation components; representational noise here is not noisy training labels.

record.problems: The near-zero training loss is qualitative, without a stated numeric value or uncertainty. The study does not report chance-level test error for the random-label networks in its own results here.
record.rows_left_out: Section 3.1 and Figures 3, A5, A9, and A10 report representational-distance comparisons. These are figure-only and do not measure a listed claim version directly, so they are not rows.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error is not measured. Training classification error is not separately reported. The common architecture and default training procedure are documented within this study; matching the original source's architecture or hyperparameters is not established.
Relative convergence time for true versus random labels and its dependence on corruption fraction.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and test error across intermediate label-corruption fractions.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels, including comparative label-learning trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its own fitting result warrants a V1 verdict despite representational similarity being its main objective. CCA distances do not measure test accuracy or label-learning order.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance is not reported as a result here; the study does not establish that architecture and training hyperparameters were unchanged relative to the original source.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 networks trained on randomized labels (group of five networks)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with one fixed random permutation of the labels shared across the group.

conditions.value: fixed random permutation, shared across networks

rows.note: The paper states that all networks trained on either unmodified or randomized-label CIFAR-10 reached near-zero training loss; this row records the randomized-label group.
rows.check: The qualitative near-zero training loss is correctly recorded. Add the architecture and training details from Appendix A.4: 11 convolutional layers with batch normalization, Adam, 100 epochs, and batch size 32. Classification error is not separately quantified.

rows.subject: CIFAR-10 networks trained on unmodified labels (group of five networks)
rows.note: Control group; the study reports near-zero training loss for all groups.
rows.check: Valid true-label control, but its training loss does not itself measure fitting random labels. Near-zero loss is observed for this control; cannot_determine refers to its ability to establish a claim version.
